name: Mad Professor
hook: A Guyanese electronics repairman in south London built his own mixing desk and carried Tubby-style dub into a second generation and a second country.

blurb.age7: He moved to London as a boy, built his own recording equipment, and used it to keep dub music going for a new generation.
blurb.age13: Neil Fraser, known as Mad Professor, moved from Guyana to London at thirteen and worked repairing electronics before building his own mixing board. In 1979 he opened Ariwa, a four-track studio in his living room, and used it to continue the version-and-echo tradition King Tubby and Lee Perry had built in Kingston, now from London.
blurb.adult: Mad Professor represents dub's diaspora phase: the technique migrating from Kingston to the UK's Jamaican community, continuing on self-built equipment rather than commercial studios, the same material condition that shaped the original Kingston scene. His work later crossed into non-reggae contexts, including a 1995 dub remix of Massive Attack's 'Protection,' carrying dub structure directly into trip-hop's toolkit.

signatureTracks.title: Dub Me Crazy! The Beginning of a New Cult
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first release in Mad Professor's long-running Dub Me Crazy series, and the record that established Ariwa's house sound.

signatureTracks.title: No Protection
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A full dub remix of Massive Attack's 'Protection' album, carrying King Tubby's structural logic directly into 1990s trip-hop.
